title.value: LitLLMs, LLMs for Literature Review: Are we there yet?
title.justification: The title is directly extracted from the beginning of the paper, indicating the focus on the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) for literature review.
title.quote: LitLLMs, LLMs for Literature Review: Are we there yet?

analysis.description: This paper explores the capabilities of recent Large Language Models (LLMs) in assisting with literature review tasks, specifically focusing on retrieval and writing of literature reviews from abstracts. It introduces a two-step search strategy combining LLM-based keyword extraction and document embedding for improved retrieval efficacy, and a planning-based generation approach to enhance the quality of literature reviews.

type.justification: The paper performs empirical analysis on the performance of LLMs for tasks related to literature review, involving experiments with retrieval and generation strategies.
type.quote: We then use this protocol to perform extensive retrieval and literature review generation experiments.

name.justification: The paper deals with tasks concerning language models, keyword extraction, and text generation, which are core to the field of Natural Language Processing (NLP).
name.quote: We explore the utility and potential of large language models (LLMs), in combination with retrieval mechanisms, to assist in generating comprehensive literature reviews for scientific papers.

name.justification: The paper proposes methods to improve paper retrieval using LLMs for literature reviews, which is directly related to Information Retrieval.
name.quote: first uses an LLM to extract meaningful keywords from the abstract of a paper and then retrieves potentially relevant papers by querying an external knowledge base.

name.justification: The generation of literature review sections using LLMs highlights the study's focus on text generation.
name.quote: To generate the literature review, we select top-k papers from the ranked list and prompt the LLM to generate the related work section based on the query abstract and the abstracts of the selected papers.

name.justification: The paper mentions using GPT-3.5-turbo in zero-shot and planned generation settings for the literature review.

is_contributed.justification: GPT-3.5 is a well-established model known prior to this paper's publication and is not introduced by this paper.
is_contributed.quote: Abstractive zero-shot baselines We use the zero-shot single-document abstractive summarizers FlanT5 (Chung et al., 2022) and LongT5 (Guo et al., 2022).

is_executed.justification: The paper demonstrates the execution of GPT-3.5-turbo in tasks related to literature review generation.
is_executed.quote: we use the closed-source models in combination with the different generation strategies (Per-cite, Sentence by sentence, plan-based, and learned plan).

is_compared.justification: GPT-3.5-turbo's performance is compared with other models like GPT-4 and Llama 2-Chat.
is_compared.quote: GPT-3.5-turbo achieve SOTA in the zero-shot setting.
